G (VII) - Cadence step pulling down into Cmaj7
E (V) - Dominant chord borrowed from A harmonic minor resolving with urgency back to Am

techniques.name: Circle of Fifths Chord Voice Leading
techniques.description: Fluidly moving through 7 distinct chord changes in a single verse progression while keeping right-hand strumming relaxed and rhythmically buoyant

notes: Cmaj7: X-3-2-0-0-0 (leave the B string open for the lush major-seventh chord)
sequence: Establish steady 4/4 folk strumming at 76 BPM
Two beats per chord for the Am - D7 and G - Cmaj7 pairs
Full measure on E major building tension before the chorus
tips: Use the common fingerings (index finger stays close to fret 1 across Am, Cmaj7, and F)
Do not rush the Dm to E change — give the E chord full resonance
Play with a warm, flexible pick for clear string definition
details.progression: Am - D7 - G - Cmaj7 - F - Dm - E

techniques.name: Single-Note Descending Bass Walkdown
techniques.description: The signature Cat Stevens acoustic piano/guitar walkdown: picking individual bass notes (C on 5th string 3rd fret, B on 2nd fret, open A string, and low G on 6th string 3rd fret) into the C chord

notes: C note: 5th string 3rd fret (3.5)
B note: 5th string 2nd fret (2.5)
A note: 5th string open (0.5)
G note: 6th string 3rd fret (3.6)
Land on open C chord strum
sequence: End the chorus line on F
Play single quarter-note descending steps: C → B → A → G
Strum full ringing C major chord on beat 1 of the new bar
tips: Fret each bass note cleanly with your fingertips
Keep the tempo steady — don't speed up through the walkdown
Accent the low G note before resolving into C

beginner.title: Master the Chorus & Bass Walkdown
steps: Learn open C, G, and F chord shapes
Practice the C - G - F chorus progression at 70 BPM
Practice the descending bass walkdown (C - B - A - G) as single notes with a metronome
Sing the famous chorus hook along with your rhythm

intermediate.title: Learn the Circle of Fifths Verse Sequence
steps: Practice the chord transitions: Am → D7 → G → Cmaj7 → F → Dm → E
Notice how Cmaj7 simply lifts your index finger from standard C
Maintain unbroken down-up strumming across all 7 chord changes
Bring the complete song up to the 76 BPM recording speed

advanced.title: Campfire Performance & Rhythmic Chops
steps: Incorporate light percussive hand muting on offbeats
Deliver the dramatic vocal dynamics from gentle verse to soaring chorus
Play the entire song from memory with fluid confidence
Lead a group sing-along around the campfire

commonMistakes: Fumbling the quick Dm to E transition at the end of the verse
Rushing the bass walkdown between chorus repetitions
Muting the open B string on Cmaj7 (make sure it rings clearly)
Strumming too aggressively — keep the groove relaxed and conversational at 76 BPM
practiceRoutine: 2 minutes: Open chord finger warm-up across Am, D7, G, and Cmaj7
5 minutes: Isolated drill of the verse cycle of fifths at 65 BPM
5 minutes: Practicing the chorus walkdown (C → B → A → G) into the C chord
5 minutes: Full run-through connecting verse into chorus
5 minutes: Singing along with the rhythm track
focusAreas: Clean chord changes through the 7-chord cycle
Dynamic acoustic volume control between verse and chorus
metronomeWork: Start at 65 BPM to lock in the verse chord transitions
Advance to 76 BPM once changes are effortless
Set metronome to clicks on beats 2 and 4 to develop natural groove
Verify tempo stability during the single-note bass walkdown
